reasons: It passes every compliance and suitability check and is available from 13 Nov 2026. 21 of 26 properties were ruled out by the checks.

explanation.headline: Oakfield Annex, room B is recommended.
reasons: No self-contained property passes the checks, so shared accommodation is considered as a last resort. It passes every other check and is available from 10 Nov 2026. 24 of 26 properties were ruled out.

It scores 78.2/100 for suitability against 66.6 for Atlas Lodge, room 3, the next option. The biggest differences are condition (grade B against grade C, +5.8 points) and facilities (shared kitchen or bathroom against shared kitchen and bathroom, +5.0 points).
cost: After housing benefit subsidy, Oakfield Annex, room B costs the temporary accommodation budget £23 a night less than Atlas Lodge, room 3 (£1,288 over the expected 56-night stay).
Oakfield Annex, room B costs the family about £96 more over the stay in travel and charges.
caveats: Shared facilities for a family: start the 6-week clock and keep searching for self-contained accommodation.
Stay planned beyond the 6-week limit for families in shared accommodation: Ombudsman remedies are typically £100–£200 a week over the limit (about £200–£400 if the stay runs to plan).

explanation.headline: Leyton Fields 2 is recommended.
reasons: It passes every compliance and suitability check and is available from 10 Nov 2026. 22 of 26 properties were ruled out by the checks.

It scores 82.3/100 for suitability against 62.8 for Seven Kings 8, the next option. The biggest differences are how much of the stay it covers (the whole stay against 22% of the stay, +6.6 points) and the longest school journey (32 min against 40 min, +5.6 points).
cost: After housing benefit subsidy, Leyton Fields 2 costs the temporary accommodation budget £5 a night more than Seven Kings 8 (£1,350 over the expected 270-night stay).
caveats: Outside the borough (Waltham Forest): notify Waltham Forest within 14 days (Housing Act 1996 s208).

explanation.headline: Cedar Court 4 is recommended.
reasons: It passes every compliance and suitability check and is available from 10 Nov 2026. 14 of 26 properties were ruled out by the checks.

It scores 97.4/100 for suitability against 83.4 for Leyton Fields 2, the next option. The biggest differences are location (in the borough against a neighbouring borough, +5.8 points) and condition (grade A against grade B, +3.8 points).
cost: After housing benefit subsidy, Cedar Court 4 costs the temporary accommodation budget £32 a night less than Leyton Fields 2 (£5,683 over the expected 180-night stay).
caveats: Gas safety certificate expires 11 Apr 2027, during the expected stay

household.notes: Eviction from private rented home (section 21 served before 1 May 2026). Grandmother does after-school childcare.

explanation.headline: Cedar Court 4 is recommended.
reasons: It passes every compliance and suitability check and is available from 10 Nov 2026. 14 of 26 properties were ruled out by the checks.

It scores 97.4/100 for suitability against 83.4 for Leyton Fields 2, the next option. The biggest differences are location (in the borough against a neighbouring borough, +5.8 points) and condition (grade A against grade B, +3.8 points).
cost: After housing benefit subsidy, Cedar Court 4 costs the temporary accommodation budget £32 a night less than Leyton Fields 2 (£5,683 over the expected 180-night stay).
caveats: Gas safety certificate expires 11 Apr 2027, during the expected stay

explanation.headline: Leyton Fields 2 is recommended.
reasons: It passes every compliance and suitability check and is available from 10 Nov 2026. 22 of 26 properties were ruled out by the checks.

It scores 82.3/100 for suitability against 62.8 for Seven Kings 8, the next option. The biggest differences are how much of the stay it covers (the whole stay against 22% of the stay, +6.6 points) and the longest school journey (32 min against 40 min, +5.6 points).
cost: After housing benefit subsidy, Leyton Fields 2 costs the temporary accommodation budget £5 a night more than Seven Kings 8 (£1,350 over the expected 270-night stay).
caveats: Outside the borough (Waltham Forest): notify Waltham Forest within 14 days (Housing Act 1996 s208).

explanation.headline: Oakfield Annex, room B is recommended.
reasons: No self-contained property passes the checks, so shared accommodation is considered as a last resort. It passes every other check and is available from 10 Nov 2026. 24 of 26 properties were ruled out.

It scores 78.2/100 for suitability against 66.6 for Atlas Lodge, room 3, the next option. The biggest differences are condition (grade B against grade C, +5.8 points) and facilities (shared kitchen or bathroom against shared kitchen and bathroom, +5.0 points).
cost: After housing benefit subsidy, Oakfield Annex, room B costs the temporary accommodation budget £23 a night less than Atlas Lodge, room 3 (£1,288 over the expected 56-night stay).
Oakfield Annex, room B costs the family about £96 more over the stay in travel and charges.
caveats: Shared facilities for a family: start the 6-week clock and keep searching for self-contained accommodation.
Stay planned beyond the 6-week limit for families in shared accommodation: Ombudsman remedies are typically £100–£200 a week over the limit (about £200–£400 if the stay runs to plan).
